question: If one of the interior angles of a regular polygon is (15)/(16) times of one of the interior angles of a regular decagon, then find the number of diagonals of the polygon.
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Interior angle of a decagon (10 sides) = (10 − 2) × 180° ÷ 10 = 144°.

Interior angle of the polygon = 15/16 × 144° = 15 × 9° = 135°.

Exterior angle = 180° − 135° = 45°.

Number of sides (n) = 360° ÷ 45° = 8.

Number of diagonals = n(n − 3) ÷ 2 = 8 × 5 ÷ 2 = 20.

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Number of sides in decagon (nd) = 10

Interior angle ratio = 15/16

**Formula Used:**

Interior Angle of a regular polygon with 'n' sides = [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n

Number of diagonals = [n(n − 3)] ÷ 2

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/0e7f8de14b766f5881073513982ff27f823191d58a9aac535dcfe94d6b5ecc47.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Interior angle of regular decagon = [(10 − 2) × 180°] ÷ 10

⇒ Interior angle of regular decagon = [8 × 180°] ÷ 10 = 144°

⇒ Interior angle of required polygon = (15/16) × 144°

⇒ Interior angle of required polygon = 15 × 9° = 135°

⇒ Let the number of sides of the polygon be 'n'

⇒ [(n − 2) × 180°] ÷ n = 135°

⇒ (n − 2) × 180 = 135n

⇒ 180n − 360 = 135n

⇒ 180n − 135n = 360

⇒ 45n = 360

⇒ n = 360 ÷ 45 = 8

⇒ Number of diagonals = [8 × (8 − 3)] ÷ 2

⇒ Number of diagonals = (8 × 5) ÷ 2 = 20

**∴ The correct answer is 20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Sum of Interior Angles

The sum of all interior angles of a polygon with 'n' sides is given by (n − 2) × 180°.

Exterior Angle Property

For any regular polygon, the exterior angle is 360° ÷ n. The sum of an interior angle and its adjacent exterior angle is always 180°.

Number of Diagonals

A diagonal is a line segment connecting two non-adjacent vertices. The formula is n(n − 3) ÷ 2. A triangle (n=3) has 0 diagonals.

Common Polygons

Pentagon (n=5, int. angle 108°), Hexagon (n=6, int. angle 120°), Octagon (n=8, int. angle 135°), Decagon (n=10, int. angle 144°).</p
